title: COMING AUGUST 1st | An Evening With…. ZOSO: The Ultimate Led Zeppelin Experience
location: Pisgah Brewing Company Black Mountain, 2948 US-70, Black Mountain, NC, 28711
description:
Saturday August 1, 2026 | GATES: 6:00PM | SHOW: 7:00PM | $31 adv. Event Details and Tickets 
  

elebrating 31 years of touring in 2026, Zoso has become one of the most iconic and respected Led Zeppelin tribute experiences in the world, having played over 4,900 shows in all 50 states and internationally. Known for their unparalleled dedication to faithfully recreating the legendary band’s live performances, Zoso has earned accolades from both critics and fans alike. 
Zoso’s live performances focus on the raw energy and intricate musicality of Led Zeppelin’s best-known hits and deeper tracks, with a particular emphasis on recreating their live show experience. The band’s commitment to authenticity has earned them praise from major outlets, with the LA Times calling them “head and shoulders above all other Led Zeppelin tributes,” and the St. Petersburg Times describing them as “the most exacting of all the Led Zeppelin tributes.” 
  
Founded in 2005, Pisgah is known for producing some of the most sought after craft ales in Western North Carolina. Pisgah Brewing Company currently operates an indoor taproom and an open air outdoor bar in the summer and fall months with live music several days a week. title: Canceled: Housing and Community Development Committee (Virtual)
UnRavel yo’self at Lower Big Hungry Falls
description:
Hendo Fun Friends
**We are the Sloth Hiking Group: “We will get there when we get there.” We dare to go where the ‘real’ hike groups don’t !!**
**This is a designated ‘silent’ Meditation Hike; we will engage quiet at the falls. But "Ooh's and Aah's" are encouraged. ”**
**https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TQ8H4EK2vt4**
I am going to unravel my stress at Lower Big Hungry Falls. Up to 12 ppl are welcome to join me.
I will spend up to 3 hours at the falls swimming, eating, reading, ponderin’ and pretending to meditate. (shorter durations optional)
**We are also doing lite clean-up maintenance.**
**Hike Details:**
Length: 1.1 mi RT (in&out); **Total descent: 325 ft (and return)**
Difficulty: Natural trail w/ rock & roots.
Drive time: 20 min
**Return Not earlier than:** 2:30 PM
Carpool contributions appreciated. $2.00 suggested
Weather Check: Hendersonville
WAITLISTED PEOPLE WILL BE ADDED AS DRIVERS SIGN ON.
(I currently have 2.5 driver(s). (=9ppl)
We suggest masks and open windows while carpooling. Only you know your own health status so judge accordingly if an event may endanger your health or the health of others.
Please bring an extra pair of shoes to avoid bringing your muddy shoes into the driver's car at the end of the hike.
Incessant prattlers will be assumed to be having an affair. Obstreperous raucous yawping is discouraged.
**THIS IS A DOG-PARTICIPANT HIKE.** This event is NOT for those who are uncomfortable with the antics of fun-loving dogs. Well trained dogs (you don’t have to yell.) can be 'off-leash'. **'On leash' during the ‘UnRavelling’ stop.** Small (lap)dogs may carpool. Large dogs will drive themselves.
**Description**;
There is a large sand beach that is popular in warm weather. ***Bring gloves. Bring 1 small grocery bag for litter pick-up..***
**Optional:** swimming in ‘brisk’ water. **Bring an inner tube float.**
Remember - hikes led by ‘the Curmudgeon’ tend to have challenging surprises. **Water sprites are mischievous in the Summer.**
We will spend up to 2 hrs at the Falls. Pack a camp-chair **there is a large sand beach.** Come prepared to meditate, practice your Tai-Chi, **森林浴**, read a book, prepare a meal, play a flute.
**UnRuffle/UnRavel:** To experience a time of quiet in a manner that you feel worthwhile. Démêlez votre stress.
Engage the 5 senses (sight, smell, touch, taste, hearing),
Observe the movement of the forest & water.
Breathe the aroma of the air, water, plants and forest.
Feel the texture of the air, water, trees and plants.
Listening to the sound of air, water, critters & birds;
Taste the air of the breezes or soothing snacks.
All hikes are at your own risk. You are responsible for your OWN safety and adequate equipment.

There are certain risks inherent in any outdoor activity. description:
Crokinole Tuesdays at Highland Brewing Taproom
Join us every Tuesday in the Taproom for an evening of flicks, strategy, and friendly competition! We’re hosting the Asheville Crokinole Club—a community of players who love this classic dexterity board game. 
Never played? No problem! Crokinole is easy to learn and endlessly fun. Players take turns flicking wooden discs across a circular board, aiming for the high-scoring center zones. The twist? If your opponent has discs on the board, you must hit one—miss, and your piece is out! 
Whether you’re a seasoned pro or just curious, come grab a pint, meet new friends, and test your skills.

description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

description:
Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall distill the pure essence of improvisational expression, converging as alchemists of sound, transmuting musical elements into their most essential forms. This quartet embodies the philosophical concept of quintessence—the fifth element beyond earth, air, fire, and water—representing the fundamental substance from which all musical reality springs. 

Their original compositions crystallize the essential qualities of diverse influences, oscillating between through-composed musical themes, groove-based soul explorations, traditional jazz-influenced pieces, Americana-inspired peaceful melodicism, world music influences, free jazz adventures, and occasional forays into cacophonous noise music. Through years of improvisational study, they’ve learned to access that rarefied space where genres dissolve into pure creative energy. 
In this musical laboratory, Sanders’ guitar becomes a conduit for universal vibration, Boyd’s reeds channel the breath of consciousness itself, Page’s bass provides the fundamental frequency of existence, while Hall’s percussion creates the rhythmic heartbeat of the cosmos.

The American dream was a song long before it was anything you could hold. It lived in parlor tunes and field hollers, in protest verses and Sunday hymns, in the things the country sang to itself to keep believing. Ghosts of the American Dream moves through that inheritance like a slow walk through rooms no one lives in anymore. A Stephen Foster lament about hard times sits beside Woody Guthrie's argument over who the land really belongs to; Sister Rosetta Tharpe's vow to study war no more leans against the breadline weariness of "Brother, Can You Spare a Dime?" These are not covers so much as visitations.

Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism
Making the Most of Difficult Situations with Modern Buddhism Teacher Sue Pepka

**Sundays 5/17-6/14 10:30am-11:45am**
Difficulties in our lives can stir up fear, frustration, and discouragement-but they can also become the fuel for real inner growth. AYPROS Lunch & Learn: Straight From the Source: NCDOR Declassified
description:
Asheville Young Professionals (AYPROS)
**AYPROS Lunch & Learn: Straight From the Source: NCDOR Declassified - FREE COWORKING DAY INCLUDED!**

**When:** Wednesday\, July 22nd\, 2026 \| 11:30 AM \- 1:00 PM
**Where:** Hatchworks Coworking, 45 S French Broad Ave, Asheville, NC
**Presented by:** Edward Shumaker, Revenue Administration Officer, North Carolina Department of Revenue

**Event Overview:**
Taxes are not exactly anyone’s favorite lunch topic. But if you run a business, freelance, manage side income, work with contractors, hire employees, or just want to understand how things work in North Carolina, knowing the basics can save you a lot of confusion later.

That’s why we’re going straight to the source.
Join AYPROS for **“Straight From the Source: NCDOR Declassified,”** an easygoing Lunch & Learn with the North Carolina Department of Revenue focused on general business tax essentials. This session is designed to make some of the common rules, forms, deadlines, and resources feel a little more approachable.

We’ll talk through the basics of:

*Reporting business income or loss*
*Common business structures and related filings*
*Sales and use tax*
*Withholding tax*
*Business registration with NCDOR*
*Filing frequencies and due dates*
*Estimated payments*
*Recordkeeping expectations*
*Common penalties and interest*
*Where to find reliable NCDOR resources when questions come up*

This is a great session for young professionals, entrepreneurs, freelancers, nonprofit leaders, managers, and anyone who wants to feel more informed about the tax side of doing business in North Carolina.

No tax background required. Just come ready to learn, ask questions, and leave with a clearer sense of what matters, what to watch for, and where to go when you need answers.

Your RSVP also includes a free coworking day at Hatchworks Coworking. Come early, stay late, and experience Asheville’s favorite downtown workspace.

**Wednesday\, July 22 \| 11:30 AM**
**Hatchworks Coworking \| 45 S\. French Broad Ave**
**Free with RSVP. Space is limited.**

This Lunch & Learn is presented by the North Carolina Department of Revenue

This session is for general educational purposes and is not a substitute for personalized legal, tax, or professional advice.

title: Shut Up & Write!® in Hendersonville
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.

When you show up, say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once you’re all settled, take some time to chat with your fellow writers. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!

**A note about the format**
We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.

For our full event schedule, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://www.shutupwrite.com).

description:
Awakening Asheville
Contact and Register: SKY Schools https://www.eventbrite.com/e/breathewithme-a-restorative-space-designed-for-the-black-community-tickets-111197697306?aff=ebdssbonlinesearch

Self-Care and Community of Practice Led by Black Facilitators, for the Black Community.

About this Event
"Caring for myself is not self - indulgence; it is self-preservation, and that is an act of political warfare." Audre Lorde

This is an invitation specifically for persons who identify as Black or African American and are overwhelmed with the injustice of the world and are ready to create space in their lives for self-care as we fight for justice for all! (We offer a parallel session for Allies to connect, learn and find support in their work to dismantle racism at allies.eventbrite.com)

We believe Black people deserve a space to relax, reassess, and realign ourselves.

We are a collective of Black stress-management & wellness instructors inspired by human values.

We are here to facilitate your journey of trauma-relief and stress-management.

Imagine how much more energy you will have and how much more powerful you will be when you cut your stress levels in half!

And it can be done in just a few minutes using nothing but your own breath...

Over the last 10 years, we've taught over 100,000 people to do just that.
The key is that your breath is directly linked to your emotions.

This 1-Hour Restorative Session Includes:
-Open, safe space for sharing and self-care for Black people
-Facilitated discussion
-Breath work and meditation

Led by Black facilitators, certified in stress and trauma relief.
Unleash the Hidden Healing Power of the Breath
-SKY Schools

**Disclaimer: In all efforts to keep this Meetup a safe space, we all agree to keep anything said within the group private and confidential.**

Do you want to take your remote working game to the next level? Do you find yourself saying wtf is Manifesting Self??

Well, you’re not alone. Remote working is glamorous, and also presents itself with challenges not seen in the traditional office environment.

We are so excited to see you, again or for the first time!

Routes-
1 miler:
RIGHT out of OLR parking lot
Continue around roundabout at Clingman, and head toward the river on Lyman St.
RIGHT on River Arts Place

3 miler:

LEFT onto W Haywood, follow all the way down to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts
Follow Roberts back to OLR
Pass OLR to Bartlett, turn around and come back to OLR

Follow Lyman back to OLR

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
We'll meet at the parking lot in front of **Haywood Appliance** and **Fresh Market** on Hendersonville Road. From there, we hop onto the Mountains-to-Sea Trail and head south for a simple out-and-back, a relatively mild 3 miles each way.

We'll take a 15-minute break at the turnaround point.

Dogs are welcome, but they must be leashed in accordance with Forest Service regulations.

**MEETING TIME & DIRECTIONS**

We'll gather at 9:00 AM on the south side of the Fresh Market parking lot in front of the Haywood Appliance store. The address is 1378 Hendersonville Rd. Look for me at my silver Hyundai.

Link for Google Maps: [Fresh Market Parking Lot](https://maps.app.goo.gl/VBNrrBeuUSnLeU3j6)

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: The Morganton Greenway Is Back! Let's Walk It!
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
We will be joining the Asheville Amblers Walking Club for their walks on the Morganton Greenway. These are free walks, although the Amblers accept donations ($4 suggested). There may also be walkers from other groups there, including AARP, Stryder, and more.

Choose between 5 KM/3.1 miles and 10 KM/6.2 miles guided walks. The walks will start in the parking lot at the end of Greenlee Ford Rd. We will meet at 8:30 for registration with step off at 9:00.

This is a pleasant walk along the Catawba River with its rapids, smooth flowing areas, grassy areas with Frisbee Golf Course, and shaded walkways. It also goes out to Freedom High School. The course is flat and paved. You may want to bring some peanuts with you as the squirrels are *very* friendly.

Dress for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. Tennis shoes should be fine. I will take a walking stick just in case, but don't expect to use it. Dogs are welcome. Strollers should be fine. As always, bring plenty of water and a protein snack.

It is likely a group of walkers will go to lunch together, perhaps at Boulevard BBQ. Feel free to join the meal.

description:
Hendo Fun Friends
**A WALK IN THE PARK.**
We will Tour de Parks of the area. One at a time.
**THIS WEEK: Perry Rudnick Nature Tr in Kellogg Preserve**
We are the Sloth Walking Team: “We will get there when we get there.”
**The Curmudgeon will lead this event. Up to 12 ppl** are welcome to join us.
**https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bsh_8qxUfDY**
Length: 1.4 mi; Accum ascent: 100 ft. Walking sticks recommended.
Drive time: 15 min
**Limited Parking; Carpooling necessary.**
Google Map = “Kellogg Nature Trails”
Apprx return time: 12 noon (=1.75hrs)
**(This event is NOT for beginners or those with health or balance issues.)**
**Optional: Some of us will lunch after the walk.**
Weather Check: Hendersonville, NC.
Carpool contributions appreciated. $1.00 suggested
Difficulty: Moderate; with roots on an earthen tr. **1 very short steep section.** Sturdy shoes suggested. Suitable for almost everyone. NOT suitable for those with balance issues.
WAITLISTED PEOPLE WILL BE ADDED AS DRIVERS SIGN ON.
I currently have 3 driver(s). (=13ppl)
We suggest open windows while carpooling. Only you know your own health status so judge accordingly if an event may endanger your health or the health of others.
Please bring an extra pair of shoes to avoid bringing your muddy shoes into the driver's car at the end of the hike.

title: In Conversation | Learning to See: Photographer Hazel Larsen Archer at Black Mountain College
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Join summer intern Sophie Weiser as she explores the incredible life and work of Hazel Larsen Archer, the first full-time photography teacher at Black Mountain College (BMC). During her nine years at BMC (1944-1953) Archer developed her unique method of “learning to see” using the camera as a tool. Weiser’s talk will also explore Archer’s experience with disability and how she navigated life on BMC Campus while producing a dazzling array of photos, including her captivating portraits of fellow BMC students and teachers, such as Josef and Anni Albers, Ruth Asawa, and Merce Cunningham.    
Bio: 
Sophie Weiser is a summer intern at the Asheville Art Museum, working with the Learning and Engagement Department’s Summer Art Camp. She is going into her third year at Trinity College Dublin, where she majors in Classics, Ancient History and Archaeology, with a focus in Classical Civilization. From the ages of three to seven she lived with her parents and twin sister in Asheville, and has continued to return to the area throughout her life. Her time in the robust local art scene of Asheville and its surrounding areas has been integral in developing her commitment to and involvement with the arts and museum world.

title: NOBODY'S DARLING STRING BAND
description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.



Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.



The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.

title: Greenwood Rye
description:
Greenwood Rye is a modern jam-grass band, formed in Nashville as the house band for the award-winning bluegrass supper club, Jane's Hideaway. Led by Shawn Spencer (Seven Handle Circus) on Guitar and Vocals, the band 's main cast features Ruth Shumway (Fiddle, Vocals), David Freeman (Mandolin, Vocals), Taylor Shuck (Banjo) & Andy Brown (Upright Bass).



The group writes fun, modern songs that are rooted in bluegrass, throwing in some jam-band tendencies, and an occasional kick-drum or delay pedal.  And they love performing fresh renditions of eclectic covers of all genres done with the beautiful sounds of acoustic bluegrass instruments.



Their latest album, "Hideaway" had a single, "Down to the River" debuted by Bluegrass Situation and two singles placed on Spotify's Official Editorial "New Grass" Playlist.  The album that was released just last August already has over 370k Spotify streams.



Recently they have been venturing further and further from Nashville, playing on festivals such as ROMP, Americanafest, Official IBMA Showcase, Albino Skunk and a slew of other small festivals, clubs, events and house concerts. 



Currently they are in residence at The Countrypolitan in Nashville, where they play every week for locals and tourists from across the country who come to Nashville looking for a great, authentic music experience. 



The residency also features regular guest appearances by some of Nashville’s greatest young bluegrass players including Frank Evans (Bronwyn Keith-Hines, Slocan Ramblers), Sasha Ostrovsky (Darius Rucker), Josey Toney(Haily Whitters), Josh Rilko (Sierra Ferrell, Lindsey Lou), Oliver Craven (Stray Birds, Sierra Ferrell), Alex Genova (Fireside Collective, Jason Carter) Tony Aichelle (Travis Tritt, Morgan Wallen), Larry Cook (Tony Trishka), Brenna MacMillan Ben Plotnick on Fiddle, Mandolin, Bass, Dobro, and Banjo.

description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
Coworking for writers in your area!
Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.

Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!

title: Sunday - Group Meditation ONLINE
description:
Asheville Meditation Meetup Group
Let's Meditate Together!

Join us for an online Sunday morning Zoom session, which includes:
\- 40 minutes unguided silent meditation \(Radiating Loving Kindness at the end\)
\- Watch a mindfulness/Buddhist information video \(25 minutes\)
\- Group Discussion/Q&A period \(20 minutes\)

Simply go to our Zoom link ahead of time and follow the prompts:

https://us02web.zoom.us/j/9742035476
Meeting ID: 974 203 5476
Passcode: 879173

Led by Founding teacher Ronya Banks or one of our trained AIM Facilitators (Kendra or Wallace).

Adults of all experience levels are welcome to attend. Meditation instruction will be given for beginners upon request.

The session begins promptly at 10:00 am. Please mute your audio unless you are sharing during the Discussion portion of the meeting.

Group Meditation Guidelines

* Arrive several minutes early. You are welcome to greet others before we start.
* Turn off your cell phones and other beeping devices.
* Sit in a comfortable position, either in your chair or cushions at home (preferably in a quiet room)
* Please mute yourself during guided meditation, and talk, and then unmute yourself to share during the discussion.
* Please remain still and do not carry your computer around, as it makes others dizzy.
* Thank you for helping us create this peaceful and safe refuge.

Meditating with others enriches and supports your practice - even online. We hope you will join us!

By Donation (Please Donate)

2. Via Website - https://www.ashevillemeditation.com/make-donation

I hope to see you there,
-Ronya Banks

description:
Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism
Dealing with Difficult Emotions with Modern Buddhism Teacher Jill Cagney

**Sundays 6/28-8/9 10:30am-11:45am**
Overwhelmed by your feelings? Buddhist psychology offers a time-tested, powerful and healthy approach to dealing with painful, challenging emotions. Each week, we will apply these methods to states like craving, anger, jealousy, and self-hatred. First, we need to recognize them, learn how they work, and accept ourselves for where we are, Next, we can disempower them using special meditations. Finally, we can envision and even experience a state of total freedom and release, having transcended these difficult emotions.

title: Modern Pop Art Experience with Michael Albert
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Join us as Michael Albert leads a Hands-On Collage workshop where participants will have the chance to create their own masterpieces using cereal boxes and other colorful cardboard packaging. All participants will receive a free signed poster of one of Albert’s creations as a special gift for joining him in this creative art making experience.  
His nationally renowned “Modern Pop Art Experience” Art programs will have toured more than 100 cities in six states this summer including: Alabama, Mississippi, Louisiana, Georgia, South Carolina & North Carolina.  Over the past 15 years he has been running this art enrichment program and brought it to more than 1,500 libraries, museums, schools, art and community centers in 48 states so far. 
American Pop Artist Michael Albert was born and raised in New York on Long Island where he graduated from New York University with a business degree. Albert is the author of an artist autobiography titled, “An Artist’s America” (Henry Holt, 2008). His work has been described as a cross between Pop Art, Cubism and Recycling.

title: Exhibition on Screen | Mary Cassatt: Painting the Modern Woman
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Mary Cassatt: Painting the Modern Woman follows the progression of Cassatt’s work, her meticulous study of the Old Masters and traditional techniques while also exposing her frustration at not finding a style that truly expressed her desire to be modern until she discovered the Impressionists. This film tells a riveting tale of great social and cultural change at a time when women were fighting for their rights and the language of art was being completely re-written. Mary Cassatt and her modern women were at the heart of it all.

title: Summer Art Camp | Art & Our Environment (Rising 3rd – 5th grade)
description:
JOIN THE WAITLIST 
Students will explore art and the environment through a series of mixed-media projects. Students will create collages of animal habitats using recycled materials and mountain landscapes featuring local wildlife. Students will be encouraged to use personal expression, gain environmental awareness, and learn creative problem-solving. Students will conclude the week by creating mixed-media memory boxes or shadow boxes filled with hand-built clay creatures.  
Meet the Instructor: Julia Worden
Julia Worden holds a master’s degree in art education and teaches visual art in Western North Carolina. She is passionate about working with learners of all ages and is dedicated to fostering confidence, critical thinking, and the development of individual artistic voices. Having spent seven years living abroad, Julia engaged extensively with galleries, artistic events, and diverse art communities across Europe, experiences she now weaves into her teaching to deepen students’ understanding and connection to art. Outside the studio and classroom, she enjoys reading, baking, and spending time with her cats, Cas and Nyx.

title: Summer Art Camp | Fun with Fiber Art (Rising 3rd - 5th grade)

Learn to weave, felt with wool, collage with paper and much more during this week focusing on fiber art! Students will explore different materials and methods of creating artworks with yarn, thread, fabric, and more!  
Meet the Instructor: M Rathsack
M Rathsack, owner and instructor at M’s School of Art, has taught many mediums in many locations for all ages in Western North Carolina since 2006. She creates her own art as the Dancing Potter working primarily as a decorative raku potter.

description:

tldr: \*\*We are at Archetype Brewing - West!\*\* Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!

🎲🍻 **Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!** 🍻🎲

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers! 🌟
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**. 🍺🎮

🔥 **Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death! 🤪

No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.*** 🏰🎉

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary. 🎭🎲
See you at the table! 🌟🍻

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

title: Kinetic Earth: Will Boyd & Kevin Spears
location: Little Jumbo: 241 Broadway St., Asheville, NC 28801
description:
Two instruments meet here that seem to have been built on opposite ends of the same planet. Kevin Spears plays the kalimba, a handful of metal tines you pluck with your thumbs, run through electronics until every note arrives as a bright, ringing point of light. Will Boyd answers on saxophones and woodwinds, all breath and wood and the low pull of the blues. Spears sends the sound upward; Boyd keeps it in orbit. The duo calls what happens between them outer space jazz, and the name they perform under, Kinetic Earth, gets at the rest: a world in motion, energy and gravity working at the same time. They bring it to Little Jumbo on Monday, July 27, another free night in the bar's curated series.

Swim at DuPont Fawn Lake
description:
Hendo Fun Friends
We are the **Sloth Hike Team of WNC**: “We will get there when we get there.” We dare to go where the ‘real’ hike groups don’t ***!!***
**https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TQ8H4EK2vt4**
I am going to unruffle my stress at Fawn Lake in DuPont Forest. Up to 16 ppl are welcome to join me.
I will spend up to 2 hours at the falls **swimming,** eating, reading and pretending to meditate.
Distance: 1.0 mi RT; 175 ft accum ascent (on the return)
Pace: **1.5mph – because I’m an ol’ Codger.**
Difficulty: gravel forest road,
Drive time: 3/4 hr/22mi 1-way
Apprx return time: 2:30 pm
Weather Check: Cedar Mountain, NC
Weather cancellations will be posted at 6:30am.
Trailhead: “Fawn Lake Access”.(10:00a)
Carpool contributions appreciated. $3.00 suggested
WAITLISTED PEOPLE WILL BE ADDED AS DRIVERS SIGN ON.
I currently have 2 driver(s) (=9ppl)
**BRING:** swim gear, swim noodles, inner tubes, picnic gear, etc. **Optional: Pack yo’ lite-weight campchair.**
We suggest slightly open windows while carpooling. Only you know your own health status so judge accordingly if an event may endanger your health or the health of others.
Please bring an extra pair of shoes to avoid bringing your muddy shoes into the driver's car at the end of the hike.
**MUST bring drying towels to place on car seats.**
Incessant prattlers will be assumed to be having an affair. Obstreperous raucous yawping is discouraged.
**THIS IS A DOG-PARTICIPANT HIKE.** This event is NOT for those who are uncomfortable with the antics of fun-loving dogs. Dogs (and Masters) required to be ‘on-leash' in DuPont. Exception for swimmers. Small (lap)dogs may carpool. Large dogs will drive themselves.
All hikes are at your own risk. You are responsible for your OWN safety and adequate equipment.

title: AYPROS Pub Club: The roof at the radical
description:
Asheville Young Professionals (AYPROS)
Join AYPROS for our July Pub Club at The Roof at The Radical, one of Asheville’s most memorable rooftop spots in the River Arts District.

Set on top of The Radical Hotel, The Roof brings together great drinks, a vibrant atmosphere, and a summer-evening setting that feels made for connecting with fellow young professionals. Whether you’re a longtime AYPROS member or attending your first event, Pub Club is designed to be a relaxed, welcoming way to spend time with good people in a memorable Asheville setting.
Pub Club is intentionally casual. Leave your business cards at home, come as you are, and enjoy an evening of conversation, camaraderie, and community without any pressure or agenda.

The evening begins at 5:00 PM. Check in, grab your first drink, and settle in for a summer night with familiar faces and new ones. This is a come-and-go event, so arrive when you can and stay as long as you’d like.

Your first drink is included thanks to our Pub Club Title Sponsor, **Allen Stahl + Kilbourne (ASK Law)**. Additional beverages and food will be available for purchase throughout the evening.
Whether you’re joining us for the rooftop atmosphere, a post-work drink, or simply a relaxed evening with other young professionals, we think this will be a perfect July Pub Club.

**What to Expect**

* A relaxed, come-and-go social atmosphere
* First drink included courtesy of ASK Law
* Additional beverages and food available for purchase
* A lively summer evening in the River Arts District
* A welcoming environment for both new and longtime AYPROS members
* No formal program, no speeches, and no pressure

**Schedule**
5:00 PM — Check-in opens, drinks, and social time
8:00 PM — Event concludes

**Location**
The Roof
The Radical Hotel
95 Roberts Street
Asheville, NC 28801

**Parking**
Street parking and nearby public parking options are available throughout the River Arts District. Please give yourself a few extra minutes to park and make your way inside.
No formal program. No speeches. No pressure. Just a beautiful Asheville setting, great conversation, and an evening spent with Asheville’s young professional community.

A special thank you to Golden Hour for welcoming AYPROS, and to Allen Stahl + Kilbourne (ASK Law) for making Pub Club possible by sponsoring everyone’s first drink.
We can’t wait to see you there.

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

WI-FI: Yes!

PARKING: Street parking in metered spots is free after 6pm. Closest municipal garages ($2/hour) are Wall St. & Coxe Street/Sears Alley.

description:

Making the Most of Difficult Situations with Modern Buddhism Teacher Sue Pepka

**Sundays 5/17-6/14 10:30am-11:45am**
Difficulties in our lives can stir up fear, frustration, and discouragement-but they can also become the fuel for real inner growth. Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.

If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.

If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge, Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work. 

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Melanie Ida Chopko: Never Had a Love Like This Album Release
description:
At long last, the release show for Melanie Ida Chopko’s newest album,’ Never Had a Love Like This’!
A rare full band show featuring Nic Jenkins (infinitikiss) on drums and special guests on bass and brass. Performing on voice and piano, Melanie weaves her music together with stories and comedy to create joy, deep feeling and a sense of togetherness. For fans of Regina Spektor, Randy Newman & Sufjan Stevens, of days without your phone and evenings on the front porch with fireflies. Come laugh and maybe cry with us! 
‘Never Had a Love Like This’ is a dispatch from modern adulthood—a sweeping indie folk record shaped by the agony of modern dating and tech-fractured intimacy. Across these ten tracks, Chopko charts a return to the body, to human connection, and to the natural world. The album is an unflinching, satisfying work from an artist who holds an entire generation’s worth of frustration and longing in her gaze to craft for us a rare gift: recognition.

“It’s rare that a songwriter truly tries to sift through the grey areas of intimacy and romance in search of meaning, but Chopko does just that. The images her resistance-melting voice and chords paint are so vivid you can almost touch them – the songs shine like a diamond.” – Americana UK

description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.



Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.



The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.

title: Jess & Jill (Full Band Show)
description:
Jesse and Jillian, aka “Jess and Jill” met on a dusty stage in Key West, Florida. Right away, there was an undeniable force of chemistry between them. Soon after meeting, they formed their musical duo, and have been playing music together nearly every day since. They have been awarded “Duo of the Year” in Key West for the past three years. 



Their musical style fits under the umbrella “Americana” with influences ranging from Jerry Garcia to Joni Mitchell to Gillian Welch and David Rawlings. They are working on an album of original music at Echo Mountain Recording in Asheville, NC. Their original music dances gleefully across the borders of genre, with one song described as “reminiscent of Pink Floyd, The Grateful Dead, and a sense of vulnerability.” Other tunes drive with zest of bluegrass, dance with a Celtic, worldly feel, and groove with a swampy, funk flavor. The thing that binds it all together? Their approach to the music as one musician - present, honest, and vulnerable.



Jesse Wagner was born in between Philadelphia and Allentown. He was raised in Telford, Pennsylvania. Jesse studied privately with Dennis Sandole, Ben Schachter, and Craig Ebener. He founded “The Happy Dog,” a band known best for their covers of The Grateful Dead, which brought him to Key West in 2011. Jesse stopped leaving Key West a few years later. 



Jillian Todd is from Potsdam, NY. Her musical background is rooted in theater and dance. Months after graduating from college in 2021, Jillian moved to Key West to work as an actor at the historic Waterfront Playhouse. Soon after moving, she was compelled to work as a musician, and devoted herself to the guitar and songwriting. 



Music 8:30-11:30pm $10 cover at the door.

Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
Coworking for writers in your area!
Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.

Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!

A note about the format
We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.

title: Walk at Little Champion Plant in Waynesville on National Ice Cream Sandwich Day
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Old Timers call this property on Old Howell Mill Road near Old Asheville Highway "Little Champion" because the Canton Champion Paper Mill put in this plant to put wax on paper for making milk cartons. The Mill changed hands several times, but the Old Timers kept calling it Little Champion. (Note that Google Maps calls it Evergreen Packaging, and the sign on the building now says Suzano.)

The 3/4-mile walking track at Little Champion runs by Richland Creek with lots of creekside trees, by fishing spots, and by a picnic area. There is a bathroom in the middle of the track. We plan to do 4 counterclockwise laps. (Yes, you are free to do fewer or even more!) That will make a total of 5 KM/3.1 miles.

Be sure you enter the property on the Old Asheville Highway (east) side of the plant (the side with the Suzano sign) on Ken Thompson Drive, go to the rear of the building, and then turning left, go ***all the way to the far end of the back of the parking lot, down by the sign designating the Drop Lot***. It is in that corner of the parking lot where we will assemble. (If you go down the stairs into the middle of the track, you will be in the wrong place and will miss where the group is assembling.)

Dress appropriately for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. There is a little hill on each lap, so some may want walking sticks. Bring **plenty of water** and a protein snack. This is a paved track, so tennis shoes will be fine. Dogs are welcome. Strollers will have no problem.

Since it is National Ice Cream Sandwich Day, at the end of the walk we will have available free ice cream sandwiches for our walkers. Now, how's that for a hot summer afternoon!

title: Fantasy and Sci-Fi Silent Book Club
description:
Asheville Introverts
BOYB - Bring Your Own Book and rant or rave about your current Fantasy or Sci-fi titles at Day Trip! We will likely be in the large ‘back room’ (with the Disco Ball and under the large white cat)

**What is a Silent Book Club?**
Referred to as "Introvert's Happy Hour", Silent Book clubs allow readers to engage with each other without the commitment of reading a shared title. Community members gather in the same place, have some casual chit chat, and then read silently together. **This group will focus on Fantasy and Sci-Fi titles (subgenres & related genres are welcome!)**

**How does it work?**
For the first 15-30 mins we will gather, grab drinks and engage in introductions. Feel free to discuss your recent favorites, mention a title that lives in your head rent free, or ask for recommendations! The best part of the Silent Book Club is being able to talk shop with other readers!

Once settled in we will dedicate 45 minutes to silent reading. Your book can be traditional, ebook, or audiobook. Read at your own pace!

Afterwards we will go around show-and-tell style and share what we read with the group. We want to know what you're reading! Organic dialogue welcome!

title: Summer Art Camp | Art & Our Environment (Rising 6th – 8th grade)
description:
REGISTER HERE 
Students will explore art and the environment through a series of mixed-media projects. Students will create collages of animal habitats using recycled materials and mountain landscapes featuring local wildlife. Students will be encouraged to use personal expression, gain environmental awareness, and learn creative problem-solving. Students will conclude the week by creating mixed-media memory boxes or shadow boxes filled with hand-built clay creatures.  
Meet the Instructor: Julia Worden
Julia Worden holds a master’s degree in art education and teaches visual art in Western North Carolina. She is passionate about working with learners of all ages and is dedicated to fostering confidence, critical thinking, and the development of individual artistic voices. Having spent seven years living abroad, Julia engaged extensively with galleries, artistic events, and diverse art communities across Europe, experiences she now weaves into her teaching to deepen students’ understanding and connection to art. Outside the studio and classroom, she enjoys reading, baking, and spending time with her cats, Cas and Nyx.

title: AVL Digital Nomads - Book Club
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**August 2026 Selection - *The Midnight Train* by Matt Haig**
[Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/Midnight-Train-Novel-World/dp/0593833376/) - [GoodReads](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/242380266-the-midnight-train)

*When your life flashes before your eyes, where would you stop?*

*No one can change the past, but the Midnight Train can take you there.*

*The chance to re-live the moments that meant most.*

*To see what kind of person you really were.*

*For Wilbur his best days were with Maggie, the love of his life. On his honeymoon in Venice.*

*Before he gave it all away.*

*He wishes he could go back and live differently. But to do so risks everything . . .*

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

**Welcome to our monthly Book Club!** We’re a small, friendly group that gets together for fun, thoughtful conversations about a different book each month.

Finished the whole book? Great. Only made it through a few chapters? Still come. Didn’t read it at all but the discussion sounds interesting? Honestly, you’re welcome too.
We meet on the **first Tuesday of every month**.

One of the best things about this group is that we keep it relatively small and guide the conversation, so it doesn’t turn into three people talking while everyone else quietly questions their life choices. Everyone has a chance to jump in, share their thoughts, and explore the book’s characters, themes, writing, and bigger ideas.

You definitely don’t need to be a literary expert. Whether you read constantly or you’re trying to get back into it, this is a relaxed place to discover new books, hear different perspectives, and meet some great people along the way.

Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.

When you show up, say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once you’re all settled, take some time to chat with your fellow writers. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!

**A note about the format**
We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.

**🤖✨ Wed Nite Special: Does AI Have a Prayer?**
with Bob Michel, RScP

📅 Wednesday, Aug 5th *(Date Changed from July 29th)*
🕡 6:30 PM
💝 Love Offering

Artificial intelligence is transforming the way we live, work, create, and communicate—but what does it mean for our spiritual lives?
Join us for an engaging and thought-provoking evening as Bob Michel, RScP, leads a fascinating exploration into the intersection of AI, consciousness, prayer, and spirituality.

Rather than focusing on fear or hype, we'll consider how artificial intelligence can serve as a valuable tool while remembering that our deepest human gifts—love, compassion, wisdom, creativity, intuition, and spiritual connection—cannot be replaced by technology.

Whether you're excited about AI, skeptical of it, or simply curious, this conversation offers a welcoming space to explore meaningful questions together.

**🌟 We'll explore topics such as:**
🤖 What role can AI play in our spiritual lives?
💭 Can technology support prayer, meditation, and personal growth?
❤️ What makes human consciousness unique?
🌎 How do we use AI wisely, ethically, and compassionately?
✨ How can we remain grounded in Spirit while embracing innovation?

Bring your questions, your curiosity, and an open mind as we reflect together on the opportunities and challenges of living thoughtfully—and spiritually—in the age of artificial intelligence.

Everyone is welcome. No prior knowledge of AI or spirituality is required—just a willingness to explore.

*We look forward to sharing this timely and inspiring conversation with you!*

#AIandSpirituality #ArtificialIntelligence #ConsciousLiving #SpiritualGrowth #CenterForSpiritualLivingAsheville #CommunityCommonsAsheville #CSLAsheville #InspiredLiving #ScienceOfMind #MindfulTechnology #ConsciousCommunity

title: Thursday Run
description:
Asheville Runners
Come run 1, 3, or 6 miles and stay for a beer and soccer tennis after at Olde London Road.

Routes-
1 miler:
RIGHT out of OLR parking lot
Continue around roundabout at Clingman, and head toward the river on Lyman St.
RIGHT on River Arts Place
Cross Riverside onto the Greenway
Right on the Greenway to the Craven St Park put in (the dock)
Turn around and go back the same way to OLR

3 miler:
Start the same as 1 miler
Continue onto Craven St. Bridge
LEFT onto Greenway after bridge
Follow Greenway all the way until it ends at Haywood Rd.
RIGHT onto Haywood Rd, go across the bridge
Cross the Roundabout at Roberts St. and continue onto Clingman
Continue on Clingman
LEFT onto Owens Bell Lane
LEFT onto Hilliard at the top of the hill
LEFT onto W Haywood, follow all the way down to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts
Follow Roberts back to OLR
Pass OLR to Bartlett, turn around and come back to OLR

6 miler:
After the W Haywood downhill to Roberts
LEFT onto Roberts St. take to Lyman and head back to the Greenway
LEFT onto the Greenway, take all the way to Amboy
RIGHT on Amboy to cross the bridge
RIGHT into French Broad River Park, run the loop at the park
Cross back over the bridge on Amboy and run the Greenway back to the roundabout
Follow Lyman back to OLR

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.
